Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(a<X<b)=P(\frac{a-\mu }{\sigma }<Z<\frac{b-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =10$ and $\sigma =4.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(10.64<X<18.28) & =P(\frac{10.64-10}{4}<Z<\frac{18.28-10}{4}) \\  & =P(0.16<Z<2.07).\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/dc1c1e8b01372821c4ad13bfb1bbfd2a102bb9d247815ace25219d3a3f42c8c2.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.16<Z<2.07) & =P(Z<2.07)-P(Z\le 0.16) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.07)-P(Z\le 0.16) \\  & =Φ(2.07)-Φ(0.16).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(2.07) & =0.9808 \\ Φ(0.16) & =0.5636\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.16<Z<2.07) & =Φ(2.07)-Φ(0.16) \\  & =0.9808-0.5636 \\  & =0.4172.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(10.64<X<18.28)=0.4172.
$$
